reconsidered_findings.corrected_reasoning: My round-1 premise was factually wrong. kaddish_chatzi.xml:34-46, the accepted maḥzor Half Kaddish, has exactly the same whole-witness guard: j:conditional with aseret-ymei-tshuva = true around the entire text, ending in j:endConditional. So the 'already done for Half Kaddish' comparison supports the current Meein Sheva encoding. It does not argue against it. On the merits, the witness prints a fixed הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ with no rubric or alternative. A guard around that phrase alone would leave a defective text outside the Ten Days, and supplying הָאֵל would add wording this witness does not print, which breaks documentary-witness policy. The whole-witness guard correctly marks this edition's text as Ten-Days-only. Ordinary-Shabbat contexts reach Meein Sheva through edition-qualified dependencies on other witnesses. In the expanded edition the first-night declarations make the Ten Days true, and the occurrence condition adds Shabbat and minyan, so the authorized use case resolves. I found no schema or guideline violation and no failing authorized use case. My round-1 objection was a preference for a different edition design, not a requirement. meein_sheva.xml's frozen hash d3fef62e… is the same as in round 1, so the file is unchanged.

reconsidered_findings.evidence: bameh_madlikin.xml:34: each numeral ב–ז is now <tei:label> and sits before its mishnah milestone. The bare terminator <milestone unit="mishnah"/> comes before the label, so the previous unit closes first. Everything stays in one tei:p, matching the single printed paragraph. A transclusion of shabbat/2/N (N≥2) now starts at the text, not at the numeral. 2:1 has no label, which matches the source, where 2:1 is unnumbered. Whether tei:label is allowed inside p here rests on the reported RNG/Schematron pass, which I did not check myself.
